clue.text: Bar offers beer, about a litre

indicators.note: about means going around, so the beer is wrapped round the litre

parts.note: bock is a strong dark German lager
L is the standard abbreviation for one litre

explanation.surface: A pub boasts of selling beer by the litre.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of chocolate or soap is also called a block: a solid rectangular piece.

clue.text: Primate hard at work overcoming phobia regularly meeting bishop

indicators.note: overcoming in a down clue puts one piece over, and here around, the others

parts.note: busy means hard at work

indicators.note: meeting joins the bishop on after the regular letters
regularly takes every other letter of phobia

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An ape toils hard to get over a fear, regularly seeing a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard at work' looks like part of the surface; it is the container word, and 'regularly' means the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'phobia'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby or galago is a small big-eyed nocturnal African primate.

clue.text: A polenta may be so served?

definitions.text: A polenta may be so served?

indicators.note: served suggests the letters being dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cornmeal dish might well be brought to the table on crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearrange A POLENTA, and that is how a polenta may be served.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is served on a dish, and the phrase also means handed over without effort.

clue.text: Do not concede order to reserve some fresh laundry?

definitions.meaning: in football, to let in no goals during a match

definitions.text: order to reserve some fresh laundry?
definitions.meaning: read literally, an instruction to set aside a freshly washed bedsheet

explanation.surface: Refusing to give way is like being told to hang on to newly washed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper who lets in no goals in a match is said to have this; the literal reading is about bedding.

clue.text: Causing dissension about point that's not serious

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for divisive goes round the point

parts.note: factious means given to faction, stirring up internal strife
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a quarrel over a remark that was only a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious remarks are flippant, joking when gravity is called for.

clue.text: The game's up: sell!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: golf is the game, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: The game is over, so cash in now.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is British slang for selling, often hawking something.

clue.text: Land girl is superficially attractive

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman working the land is merely pretty on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny goods are showy and cheap, designed to tempt buyers rather than to last.

clue.text: Be frustrated by what bad barber may do?

definitions.meaning: to be in a state of exasperation
literally, a clumsy hairdresser might rip out clumps of a customer's locks

explanation.surface: A clumsy hairdresser's work leaves a client exasperated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes extreme exasperation or anxiety; the literal sense is rough hairdressing.

clue.text: Choice brew — head spinning

indicators.note: head spinning means the leading letters turn round, the first letter trading places with the second

parts.note: a potion is a brewed drink, often magical

explanation.surface: A strong drink makes the head reel, a matter of choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head spinning' swaps the first two letters of POTION, giving OPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is an alternative one may pick, a choice.

clue.text: Fairy ring abandoned in vernal ceremony

indicators.note: abandoned means the ring letters are left out of the ceremony

parts.note: vernal means of the spring season
taken as written
a rite is a solemn ceremony

explanation.surface: A fairy ring is forsaken during a springtime ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes RING from SPRING RITE, leaving SP + RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy, a small supernatural being.

clue.text: Patsy succeeded with attack on head

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a cape or headland is a head of land jutting into the sea
go at means attack

explanation.surface: A dupe got the better of someone by striking them on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a person set up to take the blame, the classic fall guy.

clue.text: Otto getting endless stick for turning back

indicators.note: turning back means the trimmed cane is read in the opposite direction
endless means the final letter of the stick word is dropped

parts.note: a rattan is a cane walking stick made from palm stems

explanation.surface: A man named Otto swaps a broken walking stick for something to help him turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto is not a man's name here: it is a variant spelling of the rose oil. RATTAN without its end gives RATTA, which 'turning back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is an alternative name for the fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Ointment makes mark on light wood

indicators.note: in an across clue, the mark sits on, that is after, the wood

parts.note: balsa is a famously lightweight timber used in model making
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A salve leaves a stain on a piece of pale timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A balsam is a soothing aromatic resin or salve applied to the skin.

clue.text: Discard light cover, unfashionable

parts.note: a throw is a light blanket draped over furniture
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Get rid of a light bedspread because it has gone out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to get rid of it, like binning or junking it.

clue.text: Lend a frock to rock performer cutting a traditional figure

indicators.note: rock means shake about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dress is lent to a rock musician who then looks very old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting a figure' sounds like making an impression; here a figure is a dance step.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone performing country dances executes traditional figures, the set patterns of those dances.

clue.text: Noble treetop twisted into a corkscrew?

indicators.note: twisted signals the letters of the two words being wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: An aristocratic treetop has been wrung into a spiral shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is one kind of device for uncorking wine, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: In the city want bear to be beaten up

indicators.note: beaten means battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to want is to need

explanation.surface: Somebody in town wants a bear to be roughed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be beaten' reshuffles BEAR into ABER, and 'up' turns NEED into DEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, known as the Granite City.

clue.text: Replace half-crown and shilling, for example

definitions.meaning: to swap one thing for another
these pre-1971 British coins are former small change

explanation.surface: Swap out old coins such as a half-crown and a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The half-crown and the shilling were British coins withdrawn at decimalisation in 1971, so they are ex-change: former loose money.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to trade one thing for another, and the old coins were once change.

clue.text: Give up television? That could surprise the children

parts.note: jack in is British slang for quit or abandon
the box is colloquial for the TV set

explanation.surface: Banning the TV would certainly startle the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy whose clown on a spring leaps out when the lid opens, made to startle youngsters.

clue.text: Saw bachelor turning over in bed

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA

indicators.note: turning over in a down clue means the saying reads backwards

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a motto

explanation.surface: Seen: a single man tossing and turning in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of a river or sea is its bed.

clue.text: Try again to operate this key?

definitions.meaning: the Enter or carriage-... key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Pressing a keyboard key once more to make it work.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-turn it is a second go; it is also the name of the keyboard key that enters a line.

clue.text: Forcibly take too much that's picked up abroad

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: to over-seize is to grab more than one should

explanation.surface: A greedy grabber takes too much, and what is caught is from foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being in or going to foreign countries.

clue.text: One member of boating party returned to old address

indicators.note: returned means the name is written backwards

parts.note: Harris is one of the three men in Jerome K Jerome's Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: A rower comes back to a former home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old address' suggests a former home; it is an old form of addressing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic contemptuous form of address used to a man or boy, as in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Competed on track, losing the lead, and beaten at tennis

indicators.note: losing the lead means the race word drops its first letter

parts.note: raced means took part in a race on a track

explanation.surface: An athlete raced but fell behind, then lost at tennis too.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player who is aced fails to touch an unreturnable serve, so is beaten by it.

clue.text: Temperature rising in a heatwave at last, finding shade

indicators.note: in means the rising word sits inside the other letters
at last picks the final letter of heatwave

parts.note: rising means going up

explanation.surface: The temperature climbs during a heatwave until at last we find some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a colour tint, and this is a brownish-grey colour.

clue.text: Conceal wings of priory, roughly made with huge slabs

indicators.note: roughly signals the letters are thrown together in a rough new order
wings of picks the outer letters of priory

explanation.surface: Monks hide the side buildings of a priory crudely built of huge stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' shuffles CONCEAL plus PY, the wings of 'priory'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclopean masonry is built of massive irregular stones, as if by the giant Cyclopes.

clue.text: Made fast, but eating egg under supervision

indicators.note: eating means the boat word takes the egg inside it

parts.note: moored means secured, as a boat is tied up
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: Someone tied up but is still eating an egg while being watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monitored is being watched and checked, kept under observation.

clue.text: Glutton necessarily consuming a large mass

indicators.note: consuming means the two words swallow the letters, which sit within them

explanation.surface: A greedy eater inevitably puts away an enormous quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric weight of a thousand kilograms, a big mass.
